From: Tom Brooks <security@healthlynx.com>

Cc: Maya Rao <legal@healthlynx.com>
Date: 2025-10-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: No-Train Certification & Subprocessor Assurance for HLX pilot

Hi Lauren,

We're moving the HLX pilot forward and our compliance team needs a formal "no-training" certification for any data submitted to Redwood during the pilot. Specifically they asked for:

- A signed attestation that customer-provided prompts/responses will not be used to further train or improve Redwood models (including internal experiments).
- A current subprocessor inventory with access level (read/write), geographic location, and whether the subprocessors can access KV or raw prompt content.
- Details on key management (KMS/HSM), onshore/offshore access, and whether any subprocessors have cross-border access to customer data.
- Sample audit logs or a short export showing retention and deletion timestamps for ephemeral prompt artifacts.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide these items as a package (redacted where necessary)? Our legal and security teams would like the package within 10 business days; faster would be appreciated. If you have a standard attestation template we can sign, please send it over.

Thanks,
Tom Brooks
Head of Security, HealthLynx
security@healthlynx.com

--
